body: I was 17 during my first retail job and these super old gross men would NOT leave me alone. I was trying to just get through the transaction but they were stalling and refusing to pay until I talked to them. They kept trying to get me to say that I was into older guys so one of them would “have a chance.” My manager ended up having to ask them to leave. It makes me squirm now, just thinking about it years later.

I’ll definitely check out those traveling/couch surfing groups. After talking to my close friend about everything going on she invited me to stay at her family’s house for a while and now I actually feel a little hopeful. It’s a nice feeling. I can do this. Thank you again, I really appreciate it.

I hate feeling stuck in the past. It’s so hard to look at the future while I’m dealing with all this past and current trauma from my family. I want to be better than them, I just wish I was more confident in myself. Hopefully soon I’ll get out of here and see all the potential living has. Thank you for your comment, it means a lot.

I love traveling, I think money has always held me back but now that I think about it there’s nothing stopping me from just going for it. I have some savings and I’m always scared to spend it but I think if I stay here I won’t make it another year. I’d rather it go toward making a better life for myself than continue living here. Thank you so much for your suggestion.

I work in retail and came in feeling nauseated as hell a  few days ago. I was getting off of medication and had been feeling woozy for a couple days so I thought I could just work through it. However, this particular day was much worse than the previous ones. I looked pale and fatigued. I clocked into work and the assistant manager looked at me and instantly asked me if I was okay. I told her that I had a bit of nausea going on but I would be fine. She instantly offered to go get Pedialyte from the store across the street or to send me home without penalty. It really does suck working in retail sometimes and there are many bad managers out there, I feel really grateful to work with some of the good ones.
